title: Simplicial based path fibrations and boundary bijections
statement:
Use simplicial sets, horns, Kan complexes and the functor simplicial set $\operatorname{Fun}(A,K)_m=\operatorname{Hom}(A\times\Delta^m,K)$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a Kan complex $T$ with vertex $t$, let $\pi_0^s(T)$ be vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by edges. For $j\geq1$, let $\pi_j^s(T,t)$ be maps $\Delta^j\to T$ constant at $t$ on $\partial\Delta^j$ (the union of the proper faces), modulo the equivalence relation generated by homotopies $\Delta^j\times\Delta^1\to T$ constant on $\partial\Delta^j\times\Delta^1$. Fix a Kan complex $K$ and vertex $x$. Define $P_xK\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,K)$ by fixing evaluation at $0$ to be the constant simplex at $x$, let $q=\operatorname{ev}_1:P_xK\to K$, and set $\Omega_xK=q^{-1}(x)$. Write $c_x$ for the constant path. Then $q$ is a Kan fibration, $P_xK$ and $\Omega_xK$ are Kan, and $P_xK\to\Delta^0$ lifts against every boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, including $m=0$. For every $j\geq0$ the boundary construction gives a natural pointed-set bijection
$$\delta_j^s:\pi_{j+1}^s(K,x)\longrightarrow\pi_j^s(\Omega_xK,c_x),$$
where the target at $j=0$ is $\pi_0^s(\Omega_xK)$. Explicitly, for $\alpha:\Delta^{j+1}\to K$ constant at $x$ on its boundary, lift $\alpha$ to $\gamma:\Delta^{j+1}\to P_xK$ whose restriction to $\Lambda_{j+1}^{j+1}$ is constant at $c_x$, and put $\delta_j^s[\alpha]=[d_{j+1}\gamma]$. This is independent of representatives and lifts. A pointed simplicial map $(K,x)\to(K',x')$ induces maps of these path fibrations and loop fibres, and the displayed boundary bijections commute with those maps. No geometric-realization assertion is part of this statement.

No Stacks tag states this simplicial-homotopy theorem.

proof.text:
We first extract the precise lifting consequence of [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product]. Every Kan fibration lifts against every right anodyne map: it lifts against the generating horns; this property persists under a pushout by transporting the square to its attaching map, under transfinite composition by choosing successive compatible fillers and taking their colimit at limits, and under an arrow retract by composing with its section and retraction squares. Consequently, for a horn $a:\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, and any monomorphism $b:C\hookrightarrow D$, every Kan fibration lifts against
$$a\mathbin\square b:(\Lambda_i^n\times D)\cup(\Delta^n\times C)\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\times D.$$
For $i>0$, the cited product theorem makes this map right anodyne. For $i=0$, use the elementary order-reversal involution $R$ on simplicial sets: for $\alpha:[r]\to[s]$, put $\alpha^R(k)=s-\alpha(r-k)$, and give $(RX)_r=X_r$ the operators $X(\alpha^R)$. The identities $(\alpha\beta)^R=\alpha^R\beta^R$ and $R^2=1$ follow by substitution. Reversing the vertex order identifies $R\Delta^n$ with $\Delta^n$ and $R\Lambda_i^n$ with $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$; $R$ preserves degreewise unions, products and injections. Thus $R(a\square b)$ has its horn index $n>0$, and $Rp$ is still a Kan fibration because its horn problems are exactly reversed horn problems for $p$. Apply the positive-index case to $Rp$ and reverse its filler back. This proves the displayed lifting consequence for all horns, without a model structure or a realization theorem.

source.place: Theorems 3.3.1–3.3.2, pp. 81–83; Kan-specialization derived here from the existing right-anodyne product theorem, with order reversal for index zero.

proof.text:
Put $I=\Delta^1$, $E=P_xK$, $e=c_x$ and $F=\Omega_xK$. Under the internal-functor definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a horn lifting problem for
$$(\operatorname{ev}_0,\operatorname{ev}_1):\operatorname{Fun}(I,K)\to K\times K$$
is a map into $K$ on $(I\times\Lambda_i^n)\cup(\partial I\times\Delta^n)$. The inclusion of this union is the pushout-product of the horn with the monomorphism $\partial I\hookrightarrow I$, after exchanging factors. Step 1, using [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], fills it against the Kan fibration $K\to\Delta^0$. Hence the endpoint-pair map is a Kan fibration. Its pullback along $K\to K\times K$, $y\mapsto(x,y)$, is exactly $q:E\to K$. Projecting a horn square for this pullback gives a horn square for the endpoint map; its filler paired with the prescribed base simplex gives a filler for $q$. Since $K$ is Kan, a horn in $E$ is filled by first filling its image in $K$ and then lifting that simplex along $q$. A horn in $F=q^{-1}(x)$ is filled by lifting the constant base simplex $x$ along $q$. Thus both $E$ and $F$ are Kan, with the specified basepoint $e$.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.1, p. 81, and the path-space pullback in the proof of Proposition 3.6.3, p. 97.

proof.text:
A map $\partial\Delta^m\to E$ is a map $\partial\Delta^m\times I\to K$ whose value on $\partial\Delta^m\times\{0\}$ is $x$. Glue it to the constant map $x$ on $\Delta^m\times\{0\}$. The domain of this glued map is
$$(\partial\Delta^m\times I)\cup(\Delta^m\times\{0\})\subseteq\Delta^m\times I.$$
Its inclusion is the pushout-product of $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ with $\{0\}=\Lambda_0^1\hookrightarrow I$. The lifting consequence of step 1, from [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], extends it into $K$, still constantly $x$ at the initial endpoint. Transposition therefore gives an extension $\Delta^m\to E$. This holds also for $m=0$, when the original boundary is empty and the constant path $e$ is one such extension. We have proved precisely the asserted boundary lifting property for $E\to\Delta^0$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.6.3, p. 97, right lifting property of the path space against all boundaries.

proof.text:
Fix $n=j+1\geq1$ and write $H=\Lambda_n^n$. Form three simplicial sets of families using the internal-functor definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $B_n$ have $m$-simplices the maps $\alpha:\Delta^n\times\Delta^m\to K$ equal to $x$ on $\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^m$. Let $C_{n-1}$ have $m$-simplices the maps $\beta:\Delta^{n-1}\times\Delta^m\to F$ equal to $e$ on $\partial\Delta^{n-1}\times\Delta^m$. Finally, let $V_n$ have $m$-simplices the maps $\gamma:\Delta^n\times\Delta^m\to E$ equal to $e$ on $H\times\Delta^m$, and satisfying $q\gamma=x$ on $\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^m$. Operators restrict the parameter factor. Define simplicial maps
$$s:V_n\to B_n,\quad\gamma\mapsto q\gamma,\qquad r:V_n\to C_{n-1},\quad\gamma\mapsto\gamma(d_n\times1).$$
The second map lands in $F$ because $q\gamma$ is $x$ on the last face. Its boundary is $e$ because $d_n(\partial\Delta^{n-1})\subseteq H$. These facts hold also when $n=1$, where that boundary is empty and $C_0=F$.

source.place: Definition 3.4.4, p. 85, and the last-face lifting square preceding Lemma 3.4.8, pp. 87–88; the simultaneous simplicial set of lifts is introduced here.

proof.text:
The map $s:V_n\to B_n$ lifts against every $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$. Indeed, its square prescribes $\gamma$ on $\Delta^n\times\partial\Delta^m$ and $\alpha$ on $\Delta^n\times\Delta^m$. Add the constant value $e$ on $H\times\Delta^m$. These prescriptions agree on their intersection, and their image under $q$ agrees with $\alpha$, since $\alpha$ is $x$ on $\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^m$. We obtain a lifting square for $q$ with left map
$$ (H\times\Delta^m)\cup(\Delta^n\times\partial\Delta^m)\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\times\Delta^m.$$
This is the pushout-product of the last horn $H\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ with a boundary monomorphism, so [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product] and step 1 give a filler $\Gamma$. It satisfies $\Gamma=e$ on $H\times\Delta^m$ and $q\Gamma=\alpha$, hence lies in $V_n$ and solves the original square for $s$. When $m=0$, this says explicitly that every map $\alpha:\Delta^n\to K$ equal to $x$ on $\partial\Delta^n$ has a lift $\gamma:\Delta^n\to E$ with $q\gamma=\alpha$ and with $\gamma$ equal to $e$ on the whole last horn $H=\Lambda_n^n$, which is the representative used to define the boundary map.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.2, p. 82, and Lemma 3.4.8, pp. 87–88: the relative horn-prism lift, here with arbitrary simplex parameters.

proof.text:
The map $r:V_n\to C_{n-1}$ also lifts against every boundary inclusion. A lifting square gives $\gamma:\Delta^n\times\partial\Delta^m\to E$ in $V_n$ and a family $\beta:\Delta^{n-1}\times\Delta^m\to F$ extending its last-face restriction. On
$$L=(\Delta^n\times\partial\Delta^m)\cup(\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^m)$$
use $\gamma$ on the first summand; on the second summand use $e$ on $H\times\Delta^m$ and the composite $\beta:\Delta^{n-1}\times\Delta^m\to F\hookrightarrow E$ on the last face. The two face prescriptions agree because $\beta$ has boundary $e$, and they agree with $\gamma$ where the parameter is on its boundary by the lifting square and the definition of $V_n$. Thus they glue degreewise to a simplicial map $L\to E$. Step 3, with [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], makes $E\to\Delta^0$ a trivial Kan fibration: dimension zero gives its vertex-surjectivity and the other dimensions give its boundary lifts. Since $L\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\times\Delta^m$ is degreewise injective, [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] extends the glued map to $\Gamma:\Delta^n\times\Delta^m\to E$. On $\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^m$ its image under $q$ is $x$ because the last-face data lie in $F$ and the other faces are $e$. It follows that $\Gamma\in(V_n)_m$ and $r\Gamma=\beta$, as required. No subdivision or identification of a topological disk is involved.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 3.6.3, p. 97, and direct relative-boundary gluing; Stacks Tag 08NM, lemma-trivial-kan, for extension across the indicated monomorphism.

proof.text:
For any simplicial set $A$, denote its vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by edges by $c(A)$. A simplicial map $u:A\to B$ lifting against all boundaries induces a bijection $c(A)\to c(B)$: dimension zero lifts every vertex, proving surjectivity; if two chosen vertices of $A$ have images joined by an edge chain, choose lifts of the intermediate vertices and lift each edge using its two prescribed endpoints, an instance of the $\partial\Delta^1$ lifting property. This joins the chosen vertices by an edge chain in $A$, proving injectivity, including chains whose edges are traversed backwards. Apply this argument to $s$ and $r$ from steps 5 and 6. Vertices of $B_n$ are the boundary-constant $n$-simplices of $K$, and its edges are exactly their relative simplicial homotopies; hence $c(B_n)=\pi_n^s(K,x)$: its vertices are maps $\Delta^n\to K$ constant at $x$ on the boundary and its edges are maps $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to K$ constant at $x$ on $\partial\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$, exactly the generators of the equivalence relation defining $\pi_n^s(K,x)$. Likewise $c(C_{n-1})=\pi_{n-1}^s(F,e)$ for $n>1$, by the same explicit vertex and edge description with $F,e$, and $c(C_0)=\pi_0^s(F)$ for $n=1$. Therefore
$$\delta_{n-1}^s=c(r)\,c(s)^{-1}$$
is a bijection. If $\gamma$ is any lift in the question, it is a vertex of $V_n$ above $\alpha$, and this bijection sends $[\alpha]$ to $[\gamma d_n]$. The two bijections on $c(-)$ prove independence of both the representative and the lift, rather than merely proving that the basepoint has a unique preimage. Taking all families constant at $e$ proves pointedness.

source.place: Definition 3.4.4 and Lemma 3.4.8, pp. 85, 87–88; direct edge-chain comparison replaces the exact-sequence shortcut in Proposition 3.6.3.

proof.text: For a pointed map $f:(K,x)\to(K',x')$, postcomposition on $I$-families gives maps $E\to E'$ and $F\to F'$ that preserve $e$ and commute with $q$. Postcomposition therefore gives a map of the two spans $B_n\xleftarrow{s}V_n\xrightarrow{r}C_{n-1}$ and their primed analogues: it commutes strictly with $q$ and with restriction along $d_n\times1$. Applying $c(-)$ and the inverse bijections $c(s)^{-1}$ proves $f_*\delta_{n-1}^s=\delta_{n-1}^{s\prime}f_*$. For $n=1$, the fixed horn is $\Lambda_1^1=\{1\}$, so $\gamma$ is $e$ at its terminal vertex and $d_1\gamma$ is its initial vertex. Thus the construction has exactly the last-face convention of the statement in degree zero as well as in higher degrees. All arguments use only simplicial families and lifting properties.
